---
title: "Robustness of the reproduction to model settings"
author: "Simon Frost"
engine: julia
---

## Overview

The reproduction of Domínguez-García et al. (2019) rests on a reconstructed simulator. Its
settings were calibrated to match summaries of the published Dataset S1:

- half-saturation density h₀ = 0.4;
- functional-response exponent 1 + q with q = 0.3;
- no plant metabolism;
- metabolic exponent −0.25.

Two conclusions of the reproduction depend on this simulator:

- **the correlation structure:** simulated metric correlations reproduce the published three
  groups ([an end-to-end ensemble](../03_simulated_ensemble/03_simulated_ensemble.md));
- **the early-response artefact:** MR0, MAmax and Mtmax form a group only under the published,
  misaligned pulse weights ([the early response to pulse](../04_early_response/04_early_response.md)).

This vignette asks whether either conclusion changes when one setting changes. Each variant
uses the same community seeds as the baseline, so differences between them are not due to
drawing different webs.

| Variant | Setting changed | Calibrated value |
|---|---|---|
| `h0_0.2`, `h0_0.7` | half-saturation density h₀ = 0.2 or 0.7 | 0.4 |
| `q_0.6`, `q_0.1` | functional-response exponent 1 + q, q = 0.6 or 0.1 | 0.3 |
| `plant_metab` | plants pay metabolic costs | no |
| `xexp_+0.25` | metabolic exponent +0.25 | −0.25 |

```{julia}
using DominguezGarcia2019
using CSV, DataFrames, Statistics, Printf
using Plots
using Random: Xoshiro

data = joinpath(pkgdir(DominguezGarcia2019), "data")
pub = read_metrics(joinpath(data, "dominguez-garcia2019", "Dataset_S2.csv"))

# the baseline: the first 1,200 seeds of the calibrated ensemble, the seeds every variant used
base = CSV.read(joinpath(data, "simulated", "ensemble_v4.csv"), DataFrame)
base = base[in.(base.network, Ref(Set("Sim$(20191217 + k)" for k in 1:1200))), :]
# the variants were simulated with the SI's 10% global press, so the baseline uses it too
base.RM_p, base.L1DBRM_p = base.RM_p_si, base.L1DBRM_p_si
files = ["h0_0.2" => "h0_0.2", "h0_0.7" => "h0_0.7", "q_0.6" => "q_0.6",
         "plant_metab" => "plant_metabolism", "q_0.1" => "q_0.1",
         "xexp_+0.25" => "metabolic_exponent_+0.25"]
ensembles = ["baseline" => base;
             [name => CSV.read(joinpath(data, "simulated", "robustness", f * ".csv"), DataFrame)
              for (name, f) in files]]
ensembles = [name => d[5 .<= d.N .<= 99, :] for (name, d) in ensembles]
DataFrame(variant = first.(ensembles), communities = nrow.(last.(ensembles)))
```

## Some settings rarely give a viable community

A community is kept only if it reaches a locally stable equilibrium that keeps at least 90%
of its species. The number of assembly draws needed per viable community measures how open a
setting is to that rule. Three variants (h₀ = 0.7, q = 0.1 and an exponent of +0.25) were
stopped after a 90-minute budget, which explains their small samples.

```{julia}
viability = DataFrame(variant = first.(ensembles),
                      communities = nrow.(last.(ensembles)),
                      draws_per_community = [round(mean(d.attempts); digits = 1) for (_, d) in ensembles],
                      species_kept = [round(median(d.N ./ d.iniN); digits = 3) for (_, d) in ensembles],
                      plant_share = [round(median(d.Nb ./ d.N); digits = 3) for (_, d) in ensembles])
```

```{julia}
#| label: fig-draws
#| fig-cap: "Assembly draws per viable community (log scale), on the same 1,200 seeds."
bar(viability.variant, viability.draws_per_community; yscale = :log10, legend = false,
    ylabel = "draws per viable community", xrotation = 30, color = :steelblue,
    size = (700, 380), bottom_margin = 6Plots.mm, left_margin = 4Plots.mm)
```

- **h₀ = 0.2 makes assembly easier:** about 7 draws per community, against 24 for the
  baseline.
- **Plant metabolism doubles the draws, and h₀ = 0.7 needs about 13 times as many.**
- **q = 0.1 and an exponent of +0.25 almost never give a viable community:** thousands and
  hundreds of draws each, so only 6 and 9 communities were reached in the budget. The paper's
  assembly rule itself largely closes these parts of parameter space.

## The correlation structure

As in the comparison of structures across datasets, Spearman correlations are computed within
four richness bins (5–15, 16–30, 31–60 and 61–99 species) and averaged. The metric network is
then partitioned by Louvain modularity. A coarser binning than the paper's size classes is
needed because each variant has at most 1,200 communities.

```{julia}
const BINS = [(5, 15), (16, 30), (31, 60), (61, 99)]
const SIX = (:Amax, :tmax, :MRinf, :MR0, :MAmax, :Mtmax)   # the metrics with an SI version

function structure(m)
    b = [something(findfirst(r -> r[1] ≤ n ≤ r[2], BINS), 0) for n in m.N]
    m = m[b .> 0, :]
    m.N = b[b .> 0]
    sc = size_correlations(m; sizes = 1:length(BINS), max_sample = typemax(Int))
    k = length(sc.labels)
    R = [let v = filter(!isnan, sc.rho[i, j, :])
             isempty(v) ? NaN : mean(v)
         end for i in 1:k, j in 1:k]
    g, Q = modular_groups(metric_network(R); runs = 50, rng = Xoshiro(1))
    return (R = R, labels = sc.labels, groups = g, Q = Q)
end

# the metrics of one ensemble under the published or the SI's median-metric weights
function metrics(d, weights)
    d = copy(d)
    weights == "SI" && foreach(c -> (d[!, c] = d[!, Symbol(c, "_si")]), SIX)
    return prepare_metrics(d)
end

ref = structure(pub)
for k in 1:maximum(ref.groups)
    println("published group $k: ", join(ref.labels[ref.groups .== k], " "))
end
```

Each simulated structure is compared with the published one and with the baseline:

- **r(ρ):** the correlation between the 351 pairwise metric correlations;
- **mean |Δρ|:** their mean absolute difference;
- **Rand:** the agreement of the two partitions;
- **early:** whether MR0, MAmax and Mtmax fall in one group.

```{julia}
upper(R) = [R[i, j] for j in axes(R, 2) for i in axes(R, 1) if i < j]
function agreement(a, b)
    x, y = upper(a.R), upper(b.R)
    ok = isfinite.(x) .& isfinite.(y)
    return cor(x[ok], y[ok]), mean(abs.(x[ok] .- y[ok]))
end
rand_index(a, b) = mean((a[i] == a[j]) == (b[i] == b[j]) for i in eachindex(a) for j in eachindex(a) if i < j)
early(s) = length(unique(s.groups[[findfirst(==(l), s.labels) for l in ("MR0", "MAmax", "Mtmax")]])) == 1

structures = Dict((name, w) => structure(metrics(d, w)) for (name, d) in ensembles, w in ("published", "SI"))
rows = map(Iterators.product(("published", "SI"), first.(ensembles))) do (w, name)
    s = structures[(name, w)]
    d = Dict(ensembles)[name]
    r, Δ = agreement(ref, s)
    rb, _ = agreement(structures[("baseline", w)], s)
    (variant = name, weights = w, amplify = round(100mean(d[!, w == "SI" ? :MAmax_si : :MAmax] .> 1 + 1e-12); digits = 1),
     r_published = round(r; digits = 2), mean_abs_diff = round(Δ; digits = 3),
     rand_published = round(rand_index(ref.groups, s.groups); digits = 2),
     r_baseline = round(rb; digits = 2), groups = maximum(s.groups), early = early(s))
end
table = DataFrame(vec(rows))
```

`amplify` is the percentage of communities whose median pulse is amplified (MAmax > 1).

```{julia}
#| label: fig-scatter
#| fig-cap: "Pairwise metric correlations in four well-sampled variants against the published ones, under the published weights. Orange: pairs involving MR0, MAmax or Mtmax."
early_metric = [l in ("MR0", "MAmax", "Mtmax") for l in ref.labels]
pair_early = [early_metric[i] || early_metric[j] for j in eachindex(ref.labels) for i in eachindex(ref.labels) if i < j]
panels = map(["baseline", "h0_0.2", "q_0.6", "plant_metab"]) do name
    y = upper(structures[(name, "published")].R)
    x = upper(ref.R)
    p = scatter(x[.!pair_early], y[.!pair_early]; ms = 2.5, msw = 0, alpha = 0.6, color = :steelblue,
                title = name, titlefontsize = 10, legend = false, xlims = (-1, 1), ylims = (-1, 1))
    scatter!(p, x[pair_early], y[pair_early]; ms = 3, msw = 0, color = :darkorange)
    plot!(p, [-1, 1], [-1, 1]; color = :gray, ls = :dash)
end
plot(panels...; layout = (2, 2), size = (700, 640), xlabel = "published ρ", ylabel = "simulated ρ",
     guidefontsize = 8)
```

- **Where a variant can be sampled, the structure holds.** h₀ = 0.2, q = 0.6 and plant
  metabolism each give over 1,150 communities. Under the published weights they reproduce the
  published correlations about as well as the baseline does (r(ρ) 0.96–0.99, against 0.98).
  Each gives three groups close to the published ones (Rand 0.91–1.00).
- **They also agree with the baseline on the same seeds:** `r_baseline` is 0.96–0.99 under
  the published weights. Changing these settings moves the metrics, not their correlations.
- **h₀ = 0.7 (93 communities) still finds three groups**, with a weaker fit to the published
  correlations (r(ρ) 0.85, and 0.88 against the baseline), as expected from a twelfth of the
  sample.

## Where the early-response metrics go

For each partition, the table lists the metrics grouped with MAmax, and says where MR0 sits:
with MAmax, with the sensitivities to press (the group holding RM), or elsewhere.

```{julia}
members(s, l) = s.labels[s.groups .== s.groups[findfirst(==(l), s.labels)]]
function mr0_with(s)
    m = members(s, "MR0")
    "MAmax" in m && return "MAmax"
    "RM" in m && return "press sensitivities"
    return join(filter(!=("MR0"), m), " ")
end
DataFrame(variant = table.variant, weights = table.weights,
          with_MAmax = [join(filter(!=("MAmax"), members(structures[(r.variant, r.weights)], "MAmax")), " ")
                        for r in eachrow(table)],
          MR0_with = [mr0_with(structures[(r.variant, r.weights)]) for r in eachrow(table)])
```

- **Under the published weights MR0, MAmax and Mtmax share a group in every variant.**
  h₀ = 0.2 and plant metabolism give exactly the published partition. In the baseline,
  q = 0.6 and h₀ = 0.7, the extremal pulse metrics R0 and Amax join the group, much as in the
  large communities of the [early-response vignette](../04_early_response/04_early_response.md).
  With h₀ = 0.7, tmax also moves to the press group.
- **Under the SI's weights the group breaks up the same way in every well-sampled variant.**
  MAmax and Mtmax are left alone or as a pair, and MR0 joins the sensitivities to press. With
  almost no amplified median pulse, MAmax and Mtmax are nearly constant across communities, so
  they correlate with nothing.

## The early-response group follows the weights

```{julia}
#| label: fig-amplify
#| fig-cap: "Share of communities that amplify a median pulse, under the published and the SI's pulse weights."
pubw = table[table.weights .== "published", :]
siw = table[table.weights .== "SI", :]
x = 1:nrow(pubw)
bar(x .- 0.2, pubw.amplify; bar_width = 0.4, label = "published weights", color = :darkorange,
    xticks = (x, pubw.variant), ylabel = "% with MAmax > 1", xrotation = 30, size = (700, 380),
    bottom_margin = 6Plots.mm, left_margin = 4Plots.mm)
bar!(x .+ 0.2, siw.amplify; bar_width = 0.4, label = "SI weights", color = :steelblue)
```

- **In every variant the group forms under the published weights and not under the SI's.**
  The SI's weights leave 0–0.1% of communities amplifying a median pulse. This extends the
  [early-response artefact](../04_early_response/04_early_response.md) from the calibrated
  model to every setting tried.
- **Amplification depends on q; the group does not.** With q = 0.6 only 4.5% of communities
  amplify under the published weights, against 21% in the baseline, yet the group still forms.
  The misaligned weights still make MAmax and Mtmax vary between communities.
- **The two barely sampled variants say little.** With q = 0.1 and an exponent of +0.25,
  6 and 9 communities give partitions with two groups and correlations far from the published
  ones (r(ρ) 0.50 and 0.58). That MR0, MAmax and Mtmax share a group there is unsurprising
  when 27 metrics are split in two, and is not evidence either way.

## Caveats

- **One setting at a time.** Interactions between settings are untested.
- **The SI rows are compared with a structure that contains the artefact.** Their lower r(ρ)
  against the published correlations is expected and is not a failure of the variant.
- **The binning is coarser than the paper's.** Four richness bins replace the paper's three
  size classes because the variants have 1,200 communities, not 10,000.
- **Budgets, not convergence, set the small samples.** The h₀ = 0.7, q = 0.1 and +0.25 runs
  were stopped after 90 minutes; their communities are those reached in that time, so their
  composition may differ from a full run's.

## Data

The variant ensembles are in `data/simulated/robustness/` (see `data/simulated/README.md`).
They were simulated with `scripts/simulate_dataset.jl` and the setting given as `KEY=VALUE`,
and the summary in this vignette can be printed with `scripts/robustness.jl`.
